issues.description: DescriptorProto returns zero-value Import struct when imports slice is empty, not nil File
issues.detail: In ir_imports.go DescriptorProto, after the nil check, slicesx.Last returns the zero value of `imported` when files is empty, then accesses .file which is nil — that's fine, but for a non-nil but empty imports (legitimate state), this silently returns nil rather than indicating the descriptor isn't loaded. Consider documenting or guarding the empty-slice case explicitly.

issues.description: Transitive() may still panic on imports with len(files)==0 but non-nil — actually safe, but Directs uses i.publicEnd in closure on nil i
issues.detail: In Directs(), the closure captures `i` and references `i.publicEnd` and `i.weakEnd`. If i is nil, the outer guard returns an empty slice so the closure never runs — OK. But this is fragile: future readers may extend the slice and trigger nil deref. Add a brief comment noting the closure assumes i is non-nil only when slice is non-empty.

issues.description: AllMembers index counter `i` starts at 0 and increments per-call, drifting from arena IDs when f is nil
issues.detail: In ir_file.go AllMembers, when f == nil, raw is a nil iter.Seq which iterx.Map handles (no iterations), so i stays 0 — fine. But the existing behavior of incrementing `i` before wrapping seems to assume 1-based IDs; worth a comment clarifying the invariant survives the nil path.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex sentinel -1 is a behavioral change worth a CHANGELOG/breaking-change note
issues.detail: Previously ValueNodeIndex on a zero Element would presumably panic; now it returns -1. Any caller that did `e.Value().MessageKeys().At(e.ValueNodeIndex())` on a zero element will now pass -1 to At() rather than panicking upfront. The doc comment was updated, but downstream callers should be audited.

issues.description: Reflection-based test skips methods whose returns include funcs without recursing
issues.detail: In zero_test.go testZeroAny, when a returned value's Kind is reflect.Func it is silently skipped (`continue`). That means accessor methods returning closures (e.g. iter.Seq) are not validated for safe invocation on zero values. Consider at minimum invoking the iter.Seq with a no-op yield to assert it does not panic.

issues.description: Repetitive nil-guard boilerplate across File getters invites drift; consider a helper
issues.detail: ir_file.go now has ~10 near-identical `var slice []X; if f != nil { slice = f.foo }` blocks. Each new getter must remember the pattern; a tiny helper or a `(*File).safeSlice` style accessor would reduce the chance that a future getter forgets the nil check and regresses the zero-test guarantee.

review.summary: The PR adds a reflection-driven zero-value test for the `ir` package and patches getters across File, Type, Member, Oneof, Element, and imports to avoid panics on zero/nil receivers. The defensive nil checks are correct and the test design (interface-constrained generics over reflection) is reasonable. Main concerns are stylistic: significant nil-guard boilerplate in ir_file.go invites future regressions, the test skips func-returning accessors without invoking them, and ValueNodeIndex's new -1 sentinel is a subtle behavioral change worth flagging in release notes. No P0 correctness blockers identified.
